one_month_reasoning: MDB has no earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 results come in early December, after 2026-10-30. The CEO exit (Desai gave notice Sep 24; it was effective and announced Sep 28, with Ittycheria appointed interim on Sep 26), the Sep 29 Investor Day, the $1.0B buyback top-up ($1.354B remaining) and the Sep 30 PCE print that cut October hike odds are all already in the $356 close. Events inside the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, late-October hyperscaler results (a read on cloud consumption), possible news from the CEO search (a credible permanent hire helps, while more senior exits would hurt), and the buyback being put to work (a modest support). The sell side reiterated Buys (Stifel and DA Davidson, both $465) rather than downgrading, so there is no fresh flow of downgrades to extend the drop. I see no directional edge and keep a symmetric lognormal centred at about $356.5 with a monthly sigma of 16.3%. That is slightly below 71%/3.5 because the realized vol includes two event gaps that are now in the past.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods. P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 of $9.9 (1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29) x 37x = $366. EV/sales: NTM revenue of $4.1B x 7.0x = $28.7B, plus $2.6B net cash, over 85M fully diluted shares = $368. FCF yield: FY29 FCF of $0.93B at 3.3% = $28.2B, plus $2.6B, over 85M = $362. Weights are 40/35/25. The multiples sit below growth-software peers because FY27 SBC is guided at $628.9M (~21% of revenue, $7.60/share), which exceeds non-GAAP EPS of $6.39-6.58.

inputs_detail.derivation: The low end of the Investor Day '20%+ over ~3 years' target. The FY27 guide implies Q4 growth of only +14-16% ($792-810M vs $695.1M), but MDB beat its Q2 guide by ~5%, so ~20% is a fair skeptic base rather than a floor.
The midpoint of the 100-200bp/yr Investor Day target, applied to the FY27 guided ~20.8%.

FY28 op income ~$805M and FY29 ~$1,032M. Net income is ~0.89x op income (20% long-term non-GAAP tax rate plus interest income), over ~86M fully diluted shares: FY28 ~$8.3, FY29 ~$10.7. Weighted 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 (FY ends Jan 31) = ~$9.9. The supervisor confirmed this weighting.

Raised 1x from 36x after testing the supervisor's point that a typical ~5% beat puts Q3 near +25%. Still below the ~40-45x paid for ~20% software growers: FY27 SBC of $628.9M ($7.60/share) exceeds non-GAAP EPS, the CEO is interim, and the March FY28 guide has reset the stock two years running.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 $4.1B x 7.0x = $28.7B EV + $2.6B net cash, / 85M fully diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 midpoint of $3.01B grown 20%/yr gives FY28 $3.61B and FY29 $4.33B; 1/3 x 3.61 + 2/3 x 4.33 = ~$4.09B. This corrects my round-1 figure of $4.2B, which over-weighted FY29.

Today's EV is ~$26.8B ($356 x ~82M diluted shares less $2.41B cash) on ~$3.45B NTM sales, ~7.8x. I assume a modest de-rate as growth settles near 20% and Postgres/DocumentDB caps the multiple. The supervisor judged that competition a multiple cap, not a revenue cut, which is how I treat it.

inputs_detail.input: Cash and short-term investments at Jul 31, 2026

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.41B plus ~$0.7B of FCF, less ~$0.5B of buybacks that hold the fully diluted count at ~85M. This fixes the round-1 double count ($3.0B cash with a flat share count).
85.8M non-GAAP fully diluted at Q2 FY27; the $1.354B remaining authorization (~4.6% of market cap) is enough to offset SBC dilution and trim slightly.
The Investor Day target, confirmed in the deck. '>$1B FCF in FY30' is not in the deck text; it is arithmetic from the targets, so I do not use it as guidance.
90% x ~$1,032M FY29 non-GAAP op income. H1 FY27 FCF was $335.2M, or ~$670M annualized, consistent with this path.
Headline FCF is inflated by ~$630M/yr of SBC (FY27 guide $628.9M). A 3.3% headline yield is roughly a 1% SBC-adjusted yield, the most a skeptic should pay for a ~20% grower.

bear.story: The March-2027 FY28 guide comes in below ~18% growth. The FY27 guide already implies only +14-16% in Q4, and EA/other revenue (+36% in Q2 vs Atlas +29%) is lumpy term-license revenue that sets up hard comparisons. Atlas slides toward the low 20s as Postgres/DocumentDB wins new AI workloads, the CEO search drags on or senior go-to-market leaders leave, and the stock re-rates to ~5x NTM sales / ~25x EPS. This repeats the March-2026 reset to ~$216-260.

base.story: MDB keeps beating quarterly guides by a few percent, so H2 FY27 runs ~20%+ and FY28 is guided near the 20% framework. Margins expand ~150bp/yr, a credible permanent CEO is named by mid-2027, and the $1.354B remaining buyback offsets SBC dilution. The multiple stays capped near 37x NTM EPS / 7x sales by SBC quality and restrictive rates.

bull.story: Big RPO/cRPO growth converts, Atlas re-accelerates above 30% on AI workloads, a strong permanent CEO is hired, and the stock re-rates to ~9x sales, near the Stifel/DA Davidson $465 targets and the sell-side high.

thesis_break_reason: About $240 (-33%), roughly 5.5x NTM EV/sales on ~$4.1B plus cash, and back in the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone ($216-260). Getting there without a broad market crash would most likely mean the March-2027 FY28 guide fell below ~18%, confirming that the guide-implied +14-16% Q4 was not sandbagging. It could also mean Atlas slid toward 20%, or that senior leaders left during the CEO search. Any of these breaks the Investor Day 20%+ framework rather than adding event noise.

Earnings quality: FY27 SBC is guided at $628.9M (~21% of revenue) versus GAAP EPS of $0.53-0.77

reasoning: Round-2 changes. The supervisor's fact-checks led me to: (a) correct the CEO timeline from the 8-K (notice Sep 24, effective/announced Sep 28, interim appointed Sep 26); (b) relabel '>$1B FY30 FCF' as derived, not guided; (c) fix the cash/share double count ($2.6B net cash with 85M shares instead of $3.0B with 85.8M); (d) cite the buyback as $1.0B added, $2.0B aggregate and $1.354B remaining, confirmed in the Sep 25 8-K; and (e) use the correct 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 NTM weighting, which gives NTM revenue of ~$4.1B (not $4.2B) and still ~$9.9 EPS. I re-read the Q2 release myself. H1 revenue was $1,459.4M, so the FY27 guide leaves Q4 at $792-810M, +14-16%: the strongest concrete bear fact, which I now centre my bear case on. It also shows EA/other grew +36% vs Atlas +29%, so part of the 30% headline is lumpy license revenue. FY27 SBC is guided at $628.9M ($7.60/share, more than non-GAAP EPS), and the company still carries securities-litigation legal fees in its non-GAAP add-backs. On the other side, as the supervisor asked, MDB beat its Q2 guide by ~5%, the sell side reiterated Buys after the CEO exit rather than downgrading (Stifel and DA Davidson $465), and $1.354B of buyback capacity cushions the downside. So I raised the P/E multiple slightly (36x to 37x) but kept below-peer multiples. Net: fair value $366 (from $368). The EV/sales leg fell on lower NTM revenue and lower cash, the P/E leg rose on the multiple, and the FCF leg fell on lower cash. Scenario mean ~$367 (bear $220 at 27% / base $375 at 50% / bull $520 at 23%); I moved 2 points from bull to bear for the Q4 guide and March-print risk. Ladder: a lognormal with median ~$357 and sigma ~0.52, a fatter far-left tail, and P(>=356) = 0.50 (from 0.51). I stay slightly below the supervisor's $390 fair value and 0.528 because I weight SBC dilution and the March-guide base rate more heavily. That is a judgment about multiples, not a factual dispute. Research was limited to three SEC documents and one news search.
